title: SamlGroupMappingChanged
description:
`saml_group_mapping_changed` — a SAML group mapping (`kb_saml_group_mappings`: an IdP's group
value conferring a role on a team) was created or removed by a system admin. Written only by
`_admin_saml_group_mapping_write`, in the same statement as the row.

A mapping confers membership on every person the IdP asserts the group for, at each login's
reconcile, so who made one, and who removed one, is an authority record like a membership
change. The team is the event's `subject` reference. Removing a mapping deletes no membership:
the next reconcile of each member decides those.

confirmed.description:
True on a `created` that needed the admin's explicit confirmation (an `owner` role, or the
root or gating team as the target) and had it. Absent otherwise.

group_value.description: The asserted group value the mapping matches.

idp_key.description: The IdP whose assertions the mapping reads (`kb_saml_idp.idp_key`).

role.description: The role the mapping confers: as written on `created`, as it was on `removed`.

SamlGroupMappingAct.description: What happened to the mapping in a [`SamlGroupMappingChanged`] record.

oneOf.description: The mapping was removed; the memberships it conferred were left in place.

TeamRole.description:
Team role — strict hierarchy: Owner > Maintainer > Member > Watcher.

Maps directly to the `team_role` Postgres enum. Four roles is small enough
that explicit matching in SQL functions and Rust logic is clearer than a
join-table permission model.
